content: The implication diagram has incidence implying ≤, which implies both ≪ and compatibility; subdivision-order also implies ≪, and parallelism implies compatibility.
The text first counts four order relations and two symmetric relations. A slanted authorial correction challenges incidence as an order relation, describing it as transitive but nonreflexive.
Compatibility is described as reflexive, whereas self-parallelism characterizes the empty figure.

Remark a) describes recovery of incidence from ≤ by identifying strict irreducibles and invoking (1.17), then recovery of ≤ from incidence through self-incidence, deployment and inclusion. The page ends during the discussion of data fixing an atelier.
math_reading_decisions: The marginal proposal literally repeats F in every position. No G was substituted.
The rightmost letter of (1.22) is the family F in the ink, even though the preceding prose concerns the deployment of an ordinary F. H’s editorial correction is not imported.
The literal last label is (1,23). The middle character in déployement is y.
The dark diagram relation carries an extra upright component whose live/deleted state remains uncertain. This ambiguity is expressed as state alternatives in reading.tex.
The last inequality of (1.20) reads X≤F_i. H’s note correctly notices dark/retraced strokes there; no distinct underlying character or cancellation is established.
The typography of the recurring M and family F is explicitly uncertain at its first occurrence. Later instances use the first candidate.
author_doubts: Non, $\triangleleft$ n’est pas rel. d’ordre, elle est transitive mais non réflexive, car $F\triangleleft F\Longleftrightarrow F\in M$
Pour avoir une relation d’ordre il faudrait écrire [canceled $F\triangleleft$] $F\trianglelefteq F\overset{\mathrm{déf}}{\Longleftrightarrow}F\triangleleft F$ ou $F=F$.
No separate à vérifier or question mark qualifying a proof occurs on this page. The quoted marginal correction is the author’s explicit check/correction phrase.
